vocabulary.meaning_en: the form used to compare two things (usually -er)
the form for number one in a group, top or bottom (usually -est)

vocabulary.example: Cheryl was the best student in her class.
My second test was worse than the first.
I have the least money of the three.
Who lives the farthest from school?

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that does not follow the rule
vocabulary.example: "Good, better, best" is an exception to the -er/-est rule.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the basic word before endings are added

vocabulary.example: From 75% to 90% is a big improvement.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a part of a word with one vowel sound

vocabulary.example: He is the friendliest person I know.
"The #1 student" sounds awkward; say "the best student".

fine_lines.title: worse vs worst
fine_lines.explanation_ar: worse للمقارنة بين شيئين (أسوأ من). worst للتفضيل (الأسوأ في المجموعة) ويأتي مع the.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Worse" compares two things (worse than). "Worst" is the superlative (the worst in a group), used with "the".

examples.sentence: Today's weather is worse than yesterday's.
That was the worst day of the year.

fine_lines.title: less vs least
fine_lines.explanation_ar: less = أقل (مقارنة بين شيئين). least = الأقل (من بين الكل).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Less" = a smaller amount than another. "Least" = the smallest amount of all.

examples.sentence: I have less money than you.
Of the three friends, I have the least money.

fine_lines.title: the most ≠ 100%
fine_lines.explanation_ar: the most لا تعني 100%، بل أكبر كمية مقارنة بالآخرين (60% أكثر من 40%). the best تعني رقم واحد.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "The most" doesn't mean 100%; it means the biggest amount compared to others (60% is more than 40%). "The best" means number one.

examples.sentence: She had the most awards in her class.

expressions.phrase: the best student in the class
expressions.example: Cheryl was the best student in her class.
Her test had the least amount of mistakes.

expressions.phrase: How far is it to your house?
expressions.meaning_en: What is the distance to your house?
expressions.example: How far is it to your house from here?

grammar.title: Regular rule: -er and -est
grammar.explanation_ar: صيغة المقارنة غالبًا بإضافة er (bigger)، وصيغة التفضيل بإضافة est (biggest). التفضيل = رقم واحد في الأعلى أو في الأسفل.
grammar.explanation_en: Comparatives usually add -er (bigger); superlatives add -est (biggest). The superlative is number one, at the top or at the bottom.
examples: James is bigger than Mr. E.

grammar.title: Five exceptions
grammar.explanation_ar: هذه الصفات لا تتبع القاعدة: good – better – best، bad – worse – worst، many – more – most، little – less – least، far – farther – farthest.
grammar.explanation_en: These don't follow the rule: good – better – best; bad – worse – worst; many – more – most; little – less – least; far – farther – farthest.
examples: 75% is good, 90% is better, 100% is the best.
49% is bad, 39% is worse, last place is the worst.

grammar.title: Using them to fix awkward sentences
grammar.explanation_ar: بدل the #1 student قل the best student، وبدل the biggest amount of awards قل the most awards، وبدل not good قل bad، وبدل the lowest amount قل the least.
grammar.explanation_en: Instead of "the #1 student" say "the best student"; instead of "the biggest amount of awards" say "the most awards"; instead of "not good" say "bad"; instead of "the lowest amount" say "the least".
examples: Cheryl was the best student in her class.
She had only one bad mark.

grammar.title: Bonus: some two-syllable adjectives take both forms
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض الصفات ذات المقطعين تقبل الطريقتين: friendly → friendlier / more friendly، simple → simpler / more simple، gentle → gentler / more gentle. كلاهما صحيح.
grammar.explanation_en: Some two-syllable adjectives take both forms: friendly → friendlier / more friendly; simple → simpler / more simple; gentle → gentler / more gentle. Both are correct.
examples: He's the friendliest / the most friendly person I know.
This is the simplest / the most simple way.

questions.question: good → better → ___
questions.explanation_ar: صيغة التفضيل من good هي best.
questions.explanation_en: The superlative of good is best.

questions.question: "My second test was ___ than the first." (bad)
"She had the ___ awards in her class."
"That was the ___ day of my life." (very bad)
Better way to say "Cheryl was the #1 student":
"The most" means ___.
choices: the biggest amount compared to others
questions.explanation_en: The biggest amount compared to others.

questions.question: A superlative is ___.
choices: number one in a group (top or bottom)
questions.explanation_en: A superlative = number one in a group.
